Thanks Ben — this looks good. Quick answers to your questions so the plan can be scoped: 

- Target concurrency: 12 concurrent inference streams at peak (we have ~250 daily active users, bursts to 12 simultaneous clinical sessions).
- Average prompt length: 320 tokens in, expected ~180 tokens generated back (so ~500 tokens total). Occasional long cases up to 1,500 tokens.
- Latency SLO: p50 < 120ms, p95 < 350ms; TTFT ideally < 60ms for the interactive pieces.
- Mode: streaming preferred for the UI, but we also have a batch scoring job (non-real-time) used nightly. Primary focus is streaming generation (LLM chat).

Procurement: we'd like to have pricing and final MAP signed by 2026-04-20 so we can include in May budget. Procurement team (procurement@nimblehealth.com) will need an SKU-level sizing recommendation and a simple runbook for failover to lower-cost model variants.

Emily / Ben —

Thanks for the prompt details — we ran the first set of lab runs this morning against a representative 7B chat model (quantized FP16 where applicable) and an internal replication of your workload (320-in/180-out tokens avg; peak concurrency sweep to 12). Below is a concise summary; I'll attach the full CSV + our test notes.

High-level summary (streaming generation, cold start = fresh KV cache; warmed = after 10 repeated requests from same session):

- H100 (full GPU):
  - 1x concurrency: TTFT (cold) 45ms, TTFT (warmed) 20ms; p95 latency (warmed) 92ms; tokens/sec throughput 340
  - 8x concurrency: p95 latency (warmed) 160ms; sustained throughput 2,200 tokens/sec
  - 12x concurrency: p95 latency (warmed) ~260ms; occasional tail spikes to 340ms under simulated noisy background load
  - Notes: H100 gives the best TTFT and headroom for the 12-concurrency target while keeping p95 close to your SLO.

- A100 (full GPU):
  - 1x: TTFT (cold) 75ms, warmed 30ms; p95 (warmed) 140ms; throughput 260 tokens/sec
  - 8x: p95 ~240ms; throughput 1,700 tokens/sec
  - 12x: p95 ~370ms (exceeds p95 SLO in sustained burst)
  - Notes: A100 is stable but pushes p95 over your target at sustained 12x concurrency for the chosen model size.

- L40S (full GPU):
  - 1x: TTFT (cold) 65ms, warmed 28ms; p95 (warmed) 120ms; throughput 300 tokens/sec
  - 8x: p95 ~195ms; throughput 1,900 tokens/sec
  - 12x: p95 ~310ms; throughput 2,000 tokens/sec
  - Notes: L40S is close to H100 in throughput for this model family but slightly worse on TTFT; better price point in some clouds.

- MIG (fractional instances, 1/7 slice typical):
  - Per-slice TTFT/warmed p95 ~220ms at 1x, throughput ~90 tokens/sec; 12x across multiple slices adds orchestration overhead causing extra 30–80ms tail on p95 due to cross-slice synchronization and queuing.
  - Notes: MIG is cost-efficient for predictable low-concurrency workloads but will need careful autoscaling and more aggressive batching to meet p95 at 12x. We recommend full GPU or larger slice sizes for your peak interactive SLA.

Sizing recommendation for NimbleHealth (interactive streaming primary):
- Primary: H100 full GPUs in Dedicated (1 GPU per inference shard), with autoscaling to add shards at 8/12 concurrency thresholds. This hits p50/p95 and TTFT targets while leaving headroom for occasional long cases.
- Secondary: L40S as a cost-balanced fallback in another region or lower tier for non-critical batch scoring.
- MIG: acceptable for nightly batch jobs and very low-concurrency fallbacks; not recommended as main tier for interactive sessions.

Cost/throughput note: H100 unit cost is higher but yields ~25–35% fewer GPUs needed vs A100 for your traffic profile; L40S is similar throughput to H100 for this model but depends on cloud spot availability and pricing. We'll add an explicit per-month cost projection in the next pass for Dedicated sizing.
